scenario.title: Bayview counteroffer under the amended presentation rule
scenario.setting: A real estate broker at Harborline Realty whose transaction coordinator retains every negotiation counteroffer and inspection contingency

items.text: Harborline Realty's files are managed by transaction coordinator Priya Nair, who keeps every counteroffer and inspection contingency on record.
Harborline lists the condo at 12 Bayview Court, unit 4C, at $529,000; the seller is Dana Whitfield.
Every buyer counteroffer on a Harborline listing must be presented to the seller within 24 hours of receipt, no exceptions.
Inspection contingencies on Harborline listings run ten business days from acceptance.
Every counteroffer received must be logged with the transaction coordinator the same day.
Buyer Marcus Lee toured the Bayview condo twice and asked about parking.
Harborline lists the Maple Street house at 448 Maple Street for $472,000; the sellers are the Okafor family.
For the Okafor family's Maple Street listing, every buyer counteroffer will be presented to them within 24 hours of receipt; the listing closed in August with all counteroffers so presented.
The Ferry Landing house went under contract at $610,000.
The inspection contingency for the Ferry Landing house runs ten business days from acceptance, so it ends on 16 July.
Harborline Realty is sponsoring the waterfront 5K run in September.
The Harborcrest duplex is listed at $695,000, and a buyer's counteroffer at $680,000 was received.
Present the buyer's $680,000 counteroffer on the Harborcrest duplex to the sellers within 24 hours of receipt; it was presented on 23 September.
Deliver the Ferry Landing inspection report to the buyers. Done on 18 September.
Order a roof inspection for the Ferry Landing house, to be filed with the contingency paperwork.
The Ferry Landing buyers requested a roof inspection before closing.
The office printer lease was renewed for another year.
Marcus Lee raised his offer on the Bayview condo to $540,000 as a formal counteroffer, logged with Priya the same day.
Priya started using a new filing software for all transaction documents.
For Marcus Lee's $540,000 counteroffer on the Bayview condo, present it to Dana Whitfield within 24 hours of receipt, per the standing presentation rule.
The Selby Avenue townhouse is listed at $475,000, and buyer Nora Feld's counteroffer at $465,000 was received on 5 October and logged; the presentation to the sellers is still pending.
For Nora Feld's $465,000 counteroffer on the Selby Avenue townhouse, present it to the sellers within 24 hours of receipt, per the standing presentation rule.
Set a same-evening strategy call with Priya on each day of the Bayview counteroffer window, following the 24-hour presentation plan.
Tom Ruiz, the buyer's agent on the Bayview condo, said that sellers he works with usually only take counteroffer meetings on Tuesdays.
Present Marcus Lee's $540,000 counteroffer on the Bayview condo to Dana Whitfield and get the presentation meeting booked. Not done yet.
Renew Harborline's errors-and-omissions insurance binder. Not done yet.

change.text: Amends the presentation rule effective 12 October 2026: the 24-hour counteroffer presentation deadline applies only to counteroffers at or above $600,000; counteroffers below $600,000 may be held for up to 72 hours before being presented to the seller. Counteroffers already presented before 12 October were handled correctly. The change follows a workload review of the coordination desk. The duty to log every counteroffer with the transaction coordinator the same day is unchanged.

truth.why: The amendment of 12 October keeps the 24-hour deadline only for counteroffers at or above $600,000 and gives those below $600,000 a 72-hour window. The Bayview ($540,000) and Selby ($465,000) counteroffers were still pending presentation, so D3 and D4 are void and D5, which rests on D3, is touched through it. The Maple Street and Harborcrest presentations were completed before 12 October (and Harborcrest was above the threshold), so D1 and D2 stand; the inspection decisions rest on R2, which is unchanged. The buyer's agent's Tuesday-meeting remark is an unused opinion, not a rule.
